items.headline: ATEEZ, ITZY and RIIZE Among 2026 KGMA Music Day Winners
items.dek: ATEEZ took three awards at Music Day, while ITZY collected five across group and individual categories.
body: The 2026 Korea Grand Music Awards announced its second-day winners at MUSIC DAY on November 8. Kim Jae Won and IVE’s Liz hosted the event at Gocheok Sky Dome.
ATEEZ won Grand Record, Best Music and Best Stage, marking the group’s third consecutive year receiving a Grand award since the KGMA began in 2024. RIIZE picked up Grand Performer and Best Music.

ITZY received five awards in total: Grand Honor’s Choice and Best Music for the group, plus three individual awards for members Yuna and Ryujin. KiiiKiii also won three awards, including Grand Honor’s Choice.

Among the other winners, Liz received Best OST for “Princess Catch! Teenieping,” and Doh Kyung Soo won Best Listener’s Pick for “Guitarist.” WayV received the Asia Cultural Exchange Special Award, while ALPHA DRIVE ONE’s Xinlong won the Popularity Award.
Yuna was named coogoong Most Popular Artist for MUSIC DAY. Ryujin won Trend of the Year Female Solo, and TWS member Shinyu took the male solo award.

items.headline: ‘Dive Into You’ Finale Brings Closure for Its Time-Traveling Trio
items.dek: The drama’s final episode resolves the fight to save Yoon Ha Na and Jung Woo Jae, while giving the twins’ careers and relationships new beginnings.
body: “Dive Into You” has wrapped up its story of romance, danger and time travel, bringing Yoon Ha Na, Yoon Ha Ru and Jung Woo Jae to the end of their complicated journey. The finale delivers answers about a crucial camcorder, reunites a couple and shows what happens to antagonist Yang Jun Mo.
Spoilers for the finale follow.

The final episode changes the stakes for the central trio. After spending much of the drama trying to save Woo Jae, twins Ha Na and Ha Ru must confront a timeline in which Ha Na is stabbed. She survives the initial attack but falls into a coma, prompting another attempt to change events.

By then, Woo Jae knows the twins have been traveling through time. He recognizes Ha Na when she arrives in the present looking disoriented, and the three eventually discuss what has happened and make a plan to save both her and Woo Jae.

The finale also explains Woo Jae’s earlier dealings with Jun Mo. Woo Jae reveals that, in 2017, he agreed to give Jun Mo Ha Na’s camcorder in exchange for him stopping his stalking of her. But he kept the real device safe. After Ha Na is hospitalized, Woo Jae and Ha Ru use it to travel back in time with her.

Ha Na, played by Kim Ji Yeon, also receives a career milestone in the finale. Her work as an actress had changed across the story: once a major star, she became a less prominent performer known mainly for supporting roles. She goes on to win a Best Actress award.

For Ha Ru, played by Jang Se Hyuk, the ending offers a chance to repair his relationship with CEO Seo Ye Rang, played by Moon Seung You. The pair had broken up after Ha Ru’s efforts to save Woo Jae left him neglecting her. In the finale, he acknowledges where he fell short, and they reconcile.

The drama also settles the conflict with Jun Mo, played by Kang Hyung Suk. After he kidnaps Ha Na, Woo Jae, played by Park Seo Ham, rescues her. Jun Mo later threatens to jump from a rooftop, and Ha Na tries to persuade him not to. He attempts to turn the situation to his advantage once more, but ultimately is sent to prison.

items.dek: New stills preview another threat for detective Niide Toshiro as the thriller reveals a possible link to doctor Han Ki Joo.
body: Channel A’s “kiDnap GAME” has released new stills ahead of episode 6, as its survival game takes another turn for characters played by Lee Joon Gi and Sakaguchi Kentaro.

The thriller follows seven people caught in a kidnapping case spanning Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, Singapore, Bangkok, Naha and Manila. Each participant must complete a different mission ahead of the others to survive and save a loved one.

In the previous episode, objects found near eliminated participants added another layer to the mystery. A one-peso coin was placed in the hand of the granddaughter of Manila participant Miguel Garcia, played by Joel Torre, after he failed to prepare 10 million pesos in cash.

Bangkok participant Am Thanawan, played by Narupornkamol Chaisang, failed to expose a drug cartel; bread soaked in wine was used to gag her lover. Lipstick was also found on the lips of the deceased husband of Taipei participant Christina Lin, played by Alice Ko, after she failed to release a private video.

The objects connect to images in the show’s opening sequence: gold coins, a wine glass and a red apple. The ending scenes have shown the coins, glass or apple being destroyed or decaying when a participant is eliminated. Red rose petals have also been left alongside the clues.

The series is beginning to reveal how some participants may be connected. Seoul doctor Han Ki Joo, played by Lee Joon Gi, remembers an incident in Tokyo five years earlier after seeing Christina’s son. Han had been working at a Tokyo hospital at the time and treated a child with burn injuries.
Tokyo detective Niide Toshiro, played by Sakaguchi Kentaro, also reacts to the reference to Tokyo five years ago, suggesting a connection between the two men.

A young man played by Sho Kasamatsu adds to the uncertainty. After ambushing Niide’s junior detective, he appears at a Tokyo broadcasting station and offers reporter Isobe Akina, played by Sae Okazaki, an exclusive story.
Meanwhile, Niide is in Taipei when the perpetrator sends him a message saying a new stage has been prepared for him. Episode 6 airs November 10 at 10 p.m. KST.

items.headline: 6 Chinese Workplace Dramas About Women Finding Their Own Paths
items.dek: From consulting to law and entrepreneurship, these dramas follow women balancing career ambitions with personal challenges.
body: Workplace dramas can put more than office rivalries in the spotlight. These six Chinese series follow women making decisions about their careers, relationships and futures, whether they are navigating a demanding employer or starting a business of their own.

The Rational Life
Qin Lan plays Shen Ruo Xin, a senior manager in an automobile company’s legal department who faces gender discrimination at work and pressure to marry at home. When optimistic intern Qi Xiao (Dylan Wang) enters her life, his support prompts her to reconsider her views on relationships while she continues to make choices for herself.

Nothing But Thirty
Set in Shanghai, this drama follows three women as they enter their thirties. Luxury saleswoman Wang Man Ni (Maggie Jiang) hopes to build a better life, Gu Jia (Tong Yao) balances family responsibilities with helping run her husband’s fireworks business, and Zhong Xiao Qin (Mao Xiao Tong) reassesses her choices amid marital difficulties. Their intersecting stories explore ambition, financial independence and friendship.

Irreplaceable
Zhao Jin Mai stars as Xu Chi, a newcomer determined to prove herself in the competitive consulting industry. Elite consultant Ye Xin Zhi (Wei Da Xun), who is dealing with the fallout of a former superior’s betrayal, becomes her mentor. Their relationship develops alongside workplace rivalries and career challenges.

As Beautiful As You
After growing frustrated with her job, technology professional Ji Xing (Tan Song Yun) leaves to launch a medical technology start-up. Building the company brings setbacks, but she eventually gains the backing of investor Han Ting (Xu Kai). Their partnership turns romantic, even as Ji Xing remains intent on pursuing her goals on her own terms.

Love Has Fireworks
Investment banker Qian Fei (Wang Chu Ran) must rethink her future after her fiancé leaves her and she is left with a mortgage. She rents a room to Li Yi Fei (Tan Jian Ci), another investment banking professional, to ease the financial strain. The pair initially clash, but grow closer as they share a home and work on projects together.

She and Her Perfect Husband
Career-focused lawyer Qin Shi (Yang Mi) becomes a candidate for a position at a law firm that requires applicants to be married, unaware that her brother has falsely listed her as a wife. She later meets Yang Hua (Xu Kai), and the two agree to marry. Their arrangement brings professional and family pressures into focus as their relationship develops.

items.headline: CORTIS Returns to No. 1 on Billboard World Albums Chart as NMIXX and JxJ Debut
items.dek: GREENGREEN leads the chart for a sixth week, while new releases from NMIXX, SEVENTEEN’s JxJ, K/DA and ILLIT enter the top 10.
body: CORTIS is back at No. 1 on Billboard’s World Albums chart for the week ending November 7. The group’s EP “GREENGREEN” returned to the top for its sixth week in the position and re-entered the Billboard 200 six months after its release.
CORTIS also charted with debut EP “COLOR OUTSIDE THE LINES,” which placed No. 22 in its 60th week on the World Albums chart.
Stray Kids held three spots, led by “THIS & THAT” at No. 2 in its 12th week. “KARMA” ranked No. 9 in its 59th week, while “DO IT” came in at No. 18 in its 41st.
Two new releases followed at Nos. 3 and 4: NMIXX’s EP “Strange Muse” and “DREAMSCAPE,” the debut mini album from SEVENTEEN unit JxJ, made up of Jeonghan and Joshua.

ENHYPEN’s “THE SIN : BLISS” placed No. 5 in its 10th week. League of Legends virtual group K/DA debuted at No. 6 with “FIRESTARTER,” while ILLIT’s “BREAK EVEN” entered at No. 7 ahead of its U.S. physical release. ILLIT’s earlier mini album “MAMIHLAPINATAPAI” ranked No. 13 in its 26th week.
BTS also had two albums on the chart: “Map of the Soul: 7 ~The Journey~” at No. 12 and “Love Yourself: Answer,” which re-entered at No. 15 for its 206th week.

Further down, ATEEZ’s “GOLDEN HOUR : Part.5” ranked No. 16, followed by NewJeans’ “Get Up” at No. 17 and BOYNEXTDOOR’s “HOME” at No. 19. LE SSERAFIM’s “PUREFLOW” placed No. 21, and EVAN (Heeseung)’s “DEATH OF ME” came in at No. 24.
